Theme

Latin word

dūrus

dūrus, dūra, dūrum

adjective

hard, unfeeling, callous; hard, firm; tough; hard to bear, harsh; hard, harsh, unbending (of a person)

In this lexicon

  • callous

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Arch. 8: quis nostrum animō tam agrestī et dūrō fuit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 286

  • hard

    the recommended word · classical · Ov. Ars 1.476: dūra tamen mollī saxa cavantur aquā; Hor. S. 2.4.18: gallīna … dūra, a tough chicken; Traupman 325; Traupman 396

  • severe

    also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 7.8.2: dūrissimō tempore annī; Verg. A. 5.5: dūrī … dolōrēs (Lewis & Short)

  • severe

    also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 439: satis jam satis pater dūrus fuī; Ter. Ph. 497: adeōne ingeniō esse dūrō tē atque inexōrābilī …?; Traupman 150, 153, 154, 158; Traupman 325; Traupman 326; Traupman 333

Examples

  • quid magis est saxō dūrum, quid mollius undā? dūra tamen mollī saxa cavantur aquā

    what is harder than stone, what softer than water? And yet hard stones are hollowed out by soft waterOv. Ars 1.475–476
